page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, with a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512_VNNI for vector and neural network calculations, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. It also supports BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average tier performance across most metrics. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is recorded at 30983.52, while the single-core performance reaches 1865.39. Memory bandwidth tests show 1689.81 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 141.73 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Redis SET operations achieve 30.13 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 28.84 GB/sec. Notably, text generation for a small 135M LLM model registers a strong performance of 282.15 tokens per second, placing it in the top 25% tier, while prompt processing for the same model runs at 2011.18 tokens per second.

The lack of local storage and GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external storage volumes for persistent data. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides a dense memory footprint suitable for memory-bound workloads without paying for excess compute cores. This configuration is appropriate for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, medium-scale data processing, and enterprise application serving.
